item.title: Meet Clikiti Research: open data on how small-business websites treat the people who use them
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
Most people meet a local business through its website first, yet almost nobody measures those websites in the open. Clikiti Research does: 20 reports and 3,210 websites so far, free to use under CC BY 4.0. Here is why we do it, where it is going, and how to work with us.

  • Clikiti Research publishes free, open reports on small-business websites, one industry at a time: 20 reports covering 3,210 websites in its first round (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • Every report, its data and its method are free to use and cite under CC BY 4.0, as HTML, PDF, Markdown, CSV and JSON, and AI tools are welcome to read them.
  • The goal is a shared, measurable picture of how websites treat the people who use them, from contact details and accessibility to booking, forms and checkout, refreshed every quarter.

Read the post

item.title: The walk-in pitch: selling a salon website at the front desk
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
Salons and barbershops are businesses people walk into, and so can an agency. This playbook is the visit: a five-minute check on your phone outside, what to say at the desk, a leave-behind card with three numbers from our study of 193 salon websites, and the follow-up.

  • Only 42% of 193 independent hair salon and barbershop websites state a cancellation or no-show policy, and 20% say whether walk-ins are welcome (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • Among barbershops, 12% state a cancellation policy and 10% show their own work on the site, while 75% take bookings online.
  • A short visit at a quiet moment, the owner's own site on your phone and a card with three numbers is a better first approach to a salon than a cold email.

Read the post

item.title: 72% of salon websites take bookings online. 42% say what happens if you cancel.
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
Most independent salons and barbershops already have the hard part: 72% of 193 sites let a client book a chosen stylist online. What sits around that button is thin. We set the booking button beside each answer a client needs before pressing it, one pair at a time.

  • 72% of 193 independent hair salon and barbershop websites let a client book a chosen stylist or barber online, but only 42% state a cancellation or no-show policy (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • Around the button the gaps widen: 49% show a price, 26% show the salon's own work, 20% say whether walk-ins are welcome and 3% say whether a client in a wheelchair can get in.
  • Barbershops book online as often as anyone (75%) but state a cancellation policy on 12% of sites, against 55% of hair salons. For an agency the button is already built; the job is the copy around it.

item.title: The intake worksheet: nine questions to ask a wedding venue owner on the first call
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
A worksheet for the first call with an independent wedding venue: the nine questions couples ask, what to ask the owner for each one, the wording that answers it on the page, and the share of the 191 venue sites we studied that leave it out.

  • Only 9% of 191 independent wedding venue websites show which dates are still open, and 49% show a starting price (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • The worksheet takes the nine questions couples ask, in order of how rarely venue sites answer them, and gives the question to put to the owner and the wording that goes on the page.
  • The owner already answers every one of these questions by email. The call turns those emails into pages, so the agency writes them without spec work.

item.title: The inquiry email couples write because 91% of venue sites don't show open dates
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
We read 191 independent wedding venue websites the way a couple does. Each question the site leaves unanswered becomes a line in the couple's first email. Here is that email, line by line, with the share of sites that make the couple write it.

  • Only 9% of 191 independent wedding venue websites show which dates are still open (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • A typical site answers five of the nine questions couples ask before they request a tour. 51% show no starting price, 64% state no rain plan and 54% offer no way to book or request a tour online.
  • For an agency, every unanswered question is a line the couple has to email, and a reply the venue owner has to write. The fixes are mostly a page or a paragraph each.

item.title: Take the class first: a field-visit playbook for pitching an independent gym
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
Gym owners spend their day on the floor, not in their inbox. This playbook sells a gym its website the way a member finds it: check the site from the car park, book the intro through it, take the class, then talk to the owner with one page in hand. Built on four numbers from our study of 165 gym and studio websites.

  • Only 20% of 165 independent gym and fitness studio websites say where to park or whether there is childcare, and 35% state opening hours (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • 67% offer a free class, an intro, a drop-in or a day pass, but only 33% say how a membership ends.
  • Book the intro through the gym's own site, take the class, and pitch the gaps you met on the way in: that is a conversation a gym owner will have.

item.title: Four kinds of gym, four different gaps: a scouting report on 165 gym websites
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
We read 165 independent gym and studio websites the way a would-be member does. CrossFit boxes publish their timetable, boxing gyms hide the price, studios name their teachers and almost nobody says where to park. One scouting report per kind of gym, with the gap to pitch.

  • Only 20% of 165 independent gym and fitness studio websites say where to park or whether there is childcare (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • The gaps follow the kind of gym: 89% of CrossFit and functional gyms publish a class schedule against 23% of independent gyms, and 36% of boxing and martial arts gyms show a price against 81% of CrossFit gyms.
  • Scout the kind of gym before you open the site: each one has a predictable gap, and that gap is the first fix to offer.

item.title: The fine print audit: what 185 mover websites put in writing before you book
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
Only 19% of the 185 independent moving company websites we scanned say whether their estimate is binding. We audited the fine print a customer should have in writing before booking a mover, clause by clause: the carrier number, the estimate type, the rate, the coverage, the deposit and cancellation terms.

  • Only 19% of 185 independent moving company websites say whether their estimate is binding, non-binding or not-to-exceed (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • The rest of the fine print is thin too: 43% show a USDOT or MC number as text, 32% show any price, 31% explain what happens if something breaks and 24% state a deposit or cancellation terms.
  • Each clause is a paragraph or a footer line. An agency that adds all five closes the gap a customer checks before booking.

Read the post

item.title: The pitch deck in five slides: selling a website to a moving company owner
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
Only 19% of the 185 independent moving company websites we scanned say whether their estimate is binding. Here is a five-slide deck for pitching a mover, each slide built on one number from the study, with speaker notes and the slide text.

  • Only 19% of 185 independent moving company websites say whether their estimate is binding, non-binding or not-to-exceed (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • The deck has five slides, one number each: the estimate type (19%), the deposit and cancellation terms (24%, and 5% of moving and storage companies), the USDOT or MC number (43%), what happens if something breaks (31%) and the hourly rate (32%).
  • Every slide ends on a fix the owner can see the size of. Most are a paragraph of copy or a footer line; the price list is the one that takes a meeting.

item.title: What the FTC Funeral Rule asks of price lists, and what 175 funeral home websites do
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
A plain-language explainer for agencies: what the Funeral Rule requires of a funeral home's price information, what it does not say about websites, and what our study of 175 independent funeral home sites found, section by section, with each share.

  • Only 39% of 175 independent and family-owned funeral home websites publish or offer their General Price List, and 37% show a price for cremation or a burial (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • The Funeral Rule requires the price list in person and prices by phone; it does not mention websites. Cremation-focused providers show a price on 89% of their sites, one-location family homes on 17%.
  • For an agency, the price list page is the gentlest first piece of work: the home already has the list, and only 39% show it.

item.title: The letter: how to write to an independent funeral director about their website
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
A funeral director does not answer cold email sequences. This is a respectful one-page letter an agency can send instead, paragraph by paragraph: why each line is there, the four numbers from our study of 175 funeral home websites it rests on, and what to offer if the director writes back.

  • Only 39% of 175 independent and family-owned funeral home websites publish or offer their General Price List, and 37% show a price for cremation or a burial (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • 13% name a religious or cultural tradition the home serves, and 22% say a service can be watched online.
  • One page, on paper, with two numbers and one offer, is a better first approach to a funeral director than a sequence of emails.

item.title: Personal, commercial, Medicare: three kinds of insurance agency, three websites
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
We scanned 170 independent insurance agency websites. Personal lines, commercial and life, health and Medicare agencies score within three points of each other, then split hard on claims, client service and naming the companies they quote.

  • Only 39% of 170 independent insurance agency websites say how to file a claim with a number or a link (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • By kind of agency the split is wide: 56% of personal lines sites explain claims, against 40% of commercial sites and 10% of life, health and Medicare sites. Online service runs 63%, 74% and 12%.
  • The overall scores sit at 78, 78 and 75. What separates the three is what each kind of agency is asked for after the sale, and that is where an agency's pitch should start.

item.title: The referral partner pitch: reaching an insurance agency through a client you already have
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
Independent insurance agencies get much of their new business from partners: real-estate brokerages, car dealers, lenders. If you build websites for one of those partners, you are one introduction away from the agency. Here is the ask, the one-page offer and the numbers from 170 agency websites to put on it.

  • Only 22% of 170 independent insurance agency websites show a licence number, an NPN or the states the agency is licensed in (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • 40% name three or more insurance companies they quote, 39% say how to file a claim with a number or a link, and 36% show client reviews.
  • A web agency that already serves a real-estate brokerage or a car dealer can ask for an introduction to the insurance agency that client refers buyers to, and arrive with a one-page offer built on these numbers.

item.title: The season calendar: which website fix to pitch a landscaping company, month by month
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
Only 15% of the 189 independent landscaping, lawn care, hardscape and pool websites we scanned show any price. Here is a year of pitches for an agency, one fix a month, each timed to the trade's slow and busy seasons and tied to a number from the study.

  • Only 15% of 189 independent landscaping, lawn care, hardscape and pool company websites show any price: a visit, a package, a square foot or a project (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • The gaps line up with the trade's year: 51% name a seasonal plan (71% of lawn care companies, 29% of hardscape firms), 77% take a quote request online, 44% show reviews and 29% say they are licensed and insured.
  • Pitch the content jobs, prices and plans, in the slow months when the owner has time to write them; pitch quick fixes and build work while the crews are out.

item.title: The quote request form, specified: what a landscaping company should ask, and what to skip
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
77% of the 189 independent landscaping, lawn care, hardscape and pool websites we scanned take a quote request online, but only 15% show any price. Here is the estimate form field by field, with a budget picker that sits next to the company's prices instead of hiding them.

  • 77% of 189 independent landscaping, lawn care, hardscape and pool company websites take a quote request online, but only 15% show any price (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • Design and build firms are the least likely to take a request online (67%). The form below has eight fields, and the budget question is answered by the company's own published ranges, not a dropdown of guesses.
  • It is a build job of a day or two on most sites, and the price ranges beside it are the content job the owner has been putting off.

item.title: Line by line: ten patient questions on optometry websites, from 86% down to 7%
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
We read 123 independent optometry and optical boutique websites and ranked the ten questions patients ask like the lines of an eye chart. Online booking sits on the top line at 86%. A price sits on the last line at 7%.

  • Only 7% of 123 independent optometry and optical boutique websites show any price for an eye exam, a contact lens fitting or a pair of glasses (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • 86% let a patient book or request an exam online, but only 51% name a vision plan they take and 33% show what other patients say.
  • The bottom four lines of the chart (vision plans, frames, reviews, price) are where an agency's work is, and most of it is content the practice already has.

item.title: The two-week pilot: a fixed-scope website offer for an independent optometrist
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
Only 7% of 123 independent optometry websites show a price, and 49% name no vision plan. Here is a small offer an agency can put in front of a practice owner: what ships in week one, what ships in week two, and how both are measured with the study's own checks.

  • Only 7% of 123 independent optometry and optical boutique websites show any price, and only 51% name a vision plan they take (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • 44% never say whether the practice sees eye emergencies or same-day visits, and 67% show no patient reviews.
  • A two-week pilot fixes the cheapest of these first, then reruns the same pass rules, so the owner sees the before and after as checks, not opinions.

item.title: Method note: how we judged referral, insurance and price on 148 clinic sites
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
Only 18% of 148 independent physical therapy and chiropractic sites show a self-pay price. This note sets out the rules behind that number and the two next to it, with the wording that passed and the wording that did not.

  • Only 18% of 148 independent physical therapy and chiropractic clinic websites show a self-pay price for a visit or session (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • 27% say a patient can come in without a doctor's referral, and 39% name an insurance plan or say the clinic is out of network. All three are counted by fixed published rules, read from the clinic's own pages.
  • The rules are strict on purpose: "most major insurance accepted" and "$99 value" do not count. An agency can run the same tests on a prospect's site in a few minutes.

item.title: Ten questions for the first call with a physical therapy clinic owner
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
82% of 148 independent physical therapy and chiropractic sites show no self-pay price, and 73% never say whether a referral is needed. Ten questions for the first call, each tied to a finding and to what the answer tells you to build.

  • Only 18% of 148 independent physical therapy and chiropractic clinic websites show a self-pay price for a visit or session (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • The front desk already answers the missing questions on the phone: price, referral, insurance and the first visit. The first call with the owner is where you collect those answers.
  • Each of the ten questions below maps to one page or one line on the site, so the call ends with a scope, not a vague brief.

item.title: Real estate websites trail law firms on licences and fees
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
Agents and lawyers both sell trust before a decision a client can't easily undo. Set side by side, 133 independent real estate sites show a licence number on 20% and a fee on 13%; 125 small law firm sites state an admission on 43% and a consultation cost on 54%.

  • Only 20% of 133 independent real estate websites show a licence number, against 43% of 125 small law firm websites that state where their lawyers are admitted (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • Cost is the widest gap: 13% of real estate sites state a commission or management fee, and every one of the solo agent, team and luxury sites states neither; 54% of law firm sites say what a first consultation costs.
  • Real estate is level or ahead on the rest: 40% against 45% on client reviews, and 58% offer a free home valuation, the agent's version of the free consultation.

item.title: The agent page, measured: a spec for the 80% of sites with no licence number
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
80% of the 133 independent real estate websites we scanned show no licence number, and no solo agent or team site states a commission. This is one agent page, drawn to a schedule: what goes where, how big, and which client question each part answers.

  • Only 20% of 133 independent real estate websites show a real estate licence number (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • Among solo agents and small teams, 27% show a licence number, 32% a sales record, 27% client reviews and none a commission.
  • One agent page, linked from the home page, can answer all four. It is a content job of a few days, most of it spent collecting the agent's own record and reviews.

item.title: Field guide: the menu as a phone sees it, on 180 restaurant websites
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
49% of the 180 independent restaurant, café and bar websites we scanned put the menu up as real text. The rest hand a phone a PDF, a photo, an app page or nothing. Here is what each one shows a diner and a search engine, and how to check a prospect's in two minutes.

  • Only 49% of 180 independent restaurant, café and bar websites put the menu up as real text a phone can read, not a PDF or a photo (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • The text menu carries the next answers with it: 34% of the sites show prices beside dishes, and 29% mark allergens or vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free dishes, the least-answered diner question in the study.
  • Casual and family restaurants lead at 62%; cafés and bakeries trail at 36%. Moving a PDF menu onto a page is a content job, and it is the fix the rest of the menu work stands on.

item.title: The audit recording: a five-minute screen video for a restaurant owner
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
71% of the 180 independent restaurant, café and bar websites we scanned don't mark allergens or dietary dishes, and 51% don't put the menu up as text. This is the script for a short screen recording that shows an owner their own site on a phone, and the note to send with it.

  • Only 29% of 180 independent restaurant, café and bar websites mark allergens or vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free dishes, the least-answered diner question (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • 49% put the menu up as real text, 37% let a diner book a table online or say plainly it is walk-ins only, and 43% take pickup or delivery orders directly.
  • Owners are on the floor when you'd call. A five-minute screen recording of their own site on a phone, in the order a diner meets it, gets watched after service and does the pitching for you.

item.title: Teardown: the med spa site that answers all nine client questions
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
Rêvée Aesthetics in Richmond, Virginia, is the best-in-class site in our scan of 194 independent med spa and aesthetic clinic websites. We read it page by page against the study's numbers: what it does that most sites don't, and what it still leaves out.

  • Only 34% of 194 independent med spa and aesthetic clinic websites show any treatment price: per unit, per syringe, per session or a starting price (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • The best-in-class site, Rêvée Aesthetics in Richmond, Virginia, prices Botox per unit on the treatment page, names its medical director on the home page and lists each injector with a credential.
  • It still fails text contrast, as 87% of the sites do, has no medical business structured data, and stops pricing at neurotoxins.

item.title: Copy deck: the med spa consultation page, block by block
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
66% of the 194 independent med spa and aesthetic clinic websites we scanned show no treatment price, and 56% name no medical director. One consultation page can answer both, and four more client questions. Here is its finished copy, with the pitch.

  • Only 34% of 194 independent med spa and aesthetic clinic websites show any treatment price: per unit, per syringe, per session or a starting price (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • 56% name no physician as medical director or lead doctor, and 58% never explain downtime or side effects.
  • One consultation page, written from what the practice already tells clients on the phone, answers price, oversight, who treats, aftercare and the consultation itself.

item.title: 87% of accountant websites show no price: eight numbers from 158 practices
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
We read 158 independent accounting, bookkeeping, tax and advisory websites against the nine questions a new client asks. Eight numbers, itemised, no adjustments.

  • 87% of 158 independent accounting practice websites show no price, package or fee (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • Small CPA firms name a credentialed person on 80% of their sites and show a price on 3%; bookkeeping firms come close to the reverse.
  • Each gap below is rated in the report as a quick fix, a content job or a build, which makes it a line an agency can scope and price.

item.title: The one-page scope: what to send a small accounting firm after the first call
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
87% of 158 accounting practice websites show no price and 85% offer no way to book a first call online. This is the one-page proposal that turns those gaps into scope lines a small firm can approve: what each line covers, what is included and how long it takes.

  • 87% of 158 independent accounting, bookkeeping, tax and advisory practice websites show no price, package or fee (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • 77% link no working client portal and 85% offer no way to book a first consultation online; each is a scope line with a fixed deliverable.
  • Build the scope only from the questions the firm's own site fails, ordered quick fixes first, so the firm sees changes in the first week.

item.title: Inspection report: nine homeowner questions, graded across 155 pest control websites
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
We graded the websites of 155 independent pest control companies the way an inspector grades a house: clear, monitor or action. Four questions come back clear. Three need action, led by the licence number only 12% show.

  • Only 12% of 155 independent pest control company websites show a state licence number (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • Graded the way the report's own checklist grades them, four of the nine homeowner questions come back clear, two need monitoring (same-day service, 41%; safety for children and pets, 38%) and three need action: licence, price (21%) and guarantee terms (32%).
  • For an agency, the action items and the two monitor items are the pitch, and all of them are content the company already has on paper.

item.title: The safety page 62% of pest control websites don't have, before and after
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
62% of the 155 independent pest control websites we scanned say nothing about how treatment affects children or pets. Here is the page that answers it: the products used, when the family can go back in, and who does the work.

  • Only 38% of 155 independent pest control company websites say how treatment affects children or pets (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • Most of the sites that do pass use one reassurance line. A full safety page names the products, says when children and pets can go back in, and shows who is licensed to apply them (12% of sites show a licence number).
  • It is a content job built from paperwork the company already keeps: product labels, service tickets and the licence certificate.

item.title: Six beliefs about vet clinic websites, checked against 138 clinics
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
Agencies carry a few settled ideas about vet clinics: owners just phone, clinics can't post prices, every practice is full. We tested six of them against our scan of 138 independent clinic websites, one finding at a time.

  • Only 17% of 138 independent veterinary clinic websites show any price: an exam, a vaccine or a fee (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • The belief that clinics can't publish prices doesn't hold: 44% of mobile and house-call vets do, against 12% of general and family practices.
  • The phone is the one thing most sites get right (75%). The gaps an agency can sell are price, new patients, after-hours instructions and how anxious pets are handled.

Read the post

item.title: Three cold emails to a vet clinic owner, each built on one number
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
A short email sequence for agencies prospecting independent vet clinics: price, new patients and after-hours instructions, one finding from our scan of 138 clinic websites in each email, with subject lines and what to send when the owner replies.

  • Only 17% of 138 independent veterinary clinic websites show any price: an exam, a vaccine or a fee (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • The same share, 17%, say whether they are taking new patients, and 43% of general practice sites don't say what to do after hours.
  • Each gap is one email: check the clinic's own site first, send only the emails whose gap is real, and answer a reply with that clinic's three results.

item.title: The 10-minute audit: ten checks to run on a contractor's website from your phone
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
We scanned 165 independent plumbing, HVAC, electrical, roofing and appliance repair websites. Here are ten checks an agency can run on a prospect's site from a phone, in order, each with the share of sites that fail it.

  • Only 17% of 165 independent home-service trade websites state a warranty with its terms, and 18% show any price (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • 93% miss the 2.5 second load target on a phone, and 72% show no licence number as text.
  • Each check below takes about a minute on a phone, and each failed check is a line item an agency can quote.

item.title: Before and after: the emergency-first home page for an independent contractor

item.description:
The typical contractor website answers four of the nine questions homeowners ask. This is the home page that answers all nine, block by block, with sample copy and the pitch for each block.

  • Fewer than one in five state a warranty with its terms (17%) or show any price (18%), and those two answers fit on the home page in four lines.
  • The spec below is eight blocks. Most are copy changes on the template the contractor already has.

item.title: Repair shop, tire shop, body shop, car lot: where their websites part ways
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
We scanned 174 independent auto websites in four groups. Their scores sit within five points. On price, warranty, qualifications and booking, the trade each one is in decides what its site says.

  • Only 29% of 174 independent auto shop and used-car dealer websites show any price: a service, a fee, a labour rate or a car (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • 40% state a warranty with its terms, 47% name a qualification such as ASE or I-CAR, and 56% let a driver book, ask for an estimate or set up a test drive online.
  • The four kinds of business score within five points of each other. What splits them is which of these questions their trade makes easy to answer.

item.title: Talk track: getting an independent repair shop to put its prices online
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
71% of the 174 independent auto websites we scanned show no price at all. This is the conversation with the shop owner: the opener, the pushback you will hear, the numbers that answer it and what to deliver.

  • Only 29% of 174 independent auto shop and used-car dealer websites show any price: a service, a fee, a labour rate or a car (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • A shop doesn't have to quote a job it hasn't seen: a diagnostic fee or a labour rate is enough to answer the question.
  • Pair the price with the warranty (60% don't state one with terms) and the shop's qualifications (53% name none), so the price comes with the reason for it.

item.title: The eight questions clients ask a law firm website, ranked by how often they're answered
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
We scored 125 small law firm websites on the eight questions clients ask before choosing. 91% give each practice area its own page; only 43% say where their lawyers are licensed.

  • A typical small law firm website answers four of the eight questions clients ask before choosing a lawyer, across 125 sites scanned (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • 91% give each practice area its own page, but only 43% say where their lawyers are licensed and 45% show client reviews.
  • The four least-answered questions sit between 39% and 46%, and three of them are rated quick fixes in the report.

item.description:
72% of the 135 independent dental practice websites we scanned don't say which insurance they take. Here is the page to build, section by section, with copy the practice can adapt.

item.title: Only 9% of private school websites let a parent reach a person in one tap
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
It's the cheapest fix in our scan of 114 schools and tutoring centres, and almost every one misses it. That makes it the easiest way to open a pitch.

  • Only 9% of 114 private school and tutoring websites make phone and email tappable and state office hours (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • It's the least-answered of the six questions parents ask before choosing a school.
  • The fix takes about an hour, which makes it a low-risk first project to pitch.

item.title: 4 in 5 private school websites fail a basic readability test
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
80% of the 114 school and tutoring websites we scanned have text below the 4.5:1 contrast minimum. On most sites it's a theme setting, not a redesign.

  • 80% of 114 private school and tutoring websites fail the WCAG 1.4.3 text contrast minimum of 4.5:1 (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • 57% take longer than 2.5 seconds to show their main content on a phone.
  • Contrast is usually fixed in the theme's colour settings, so it makes a quick first project.

item.title: Only 28% of dental practice websites say which insurance they take
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
It's the first question a new patient has, and 72% of the 135 independent practices we scanned make them call to ask. Prices and new-patient status are missing even more often.

  • Only 28% of 135 independent dental practice websites say which insurance they take (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • Fewer still say what a visit costs (23%) or whether they're taking new patients (22%).
  • 79% state their opening hours, so practices can publish facts; they just leave out the ones patients ask first.

item.title: Most small law firm websites can't tell a client whether anyone will answer tonight
item.dc:creator: Clikiti Research
item.description:
Only 39% of the 125 small law firm websites we scanned pair a tappable phone number with office hours, 24/7 availability or a response time. One line in the header fixes it.

  • Only 39% of 125 small law firm websites pair a tappable phone number with office hours, 24/7 availability or a response time (Clikiti Research, October 2026).
  • Only 43% say where their lawyers are admitted to practise.
  • Both are quick fixes, which makes them an easy first project for an agency.
